walkthroughs.body_html:
Without O₂, the ETC stops. NADH and FADH₂ build up — NAD runs out.

If NAD isn't regenerated, glycolysis stops too → no ATP at all.

Anaerobic respiration's whole point: regenerate NAD from NADH so glycolysis can keep producing 2 ATP per glucose.

In mammalian muscle:
pyruvate + NADH → lactate + NAD
(catalysed by lactate dehydrogenase)

Lactate builds up → muscle fatigue. Later sent to liver, oxidised back to pyruvate (oxygen debt).

In yeast:
pyruvate → CO₂ + ethanal → ethanol + NAD
Used in brewing and breadmaking. Irreversible — no debt.

Cells can respire different substrates:
- Carbohydrate — preferred, fast
- Lipid — fatty acids broken into acetyl groups → Krebs. Per gram, ~2× the ATP of carbs
- Protein — last resort; amino acids deaminated

Respiratory quotient (RQ) = CO₂ produced ÷ O₂ used.
- Carbs RQ ≈ 1.0
- Lipids RQ ≈ 0.7
- Proteins RQ ≈ 0.9

RQ > 1 → anaerobic respiration contributing.
